analysis:
Examined the changed CI workflow (.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml), the new changelog fragment, and doc updates in docs/developer/build.md and docs/developer/test.md. The PR touches only CI/advisory review tooling and documentation; no provider code, WebSocket contract (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), keys, attestation or cache paths are changed, so no canonical threat-model assets or threats are affected.

Workflow security-relevant changes: (1) The maintainer-dispatch path is removed (pr_number input, Resolve maintainer-requested PR step, workflow_dispatch in the review job `if`, and the dispatch clause in BEDROCK_SCAN_ENABLED). This reduces attack surface and paid-call exposure. The preflight input now defaults to true and the review job runs only on pull_request_target, so dispatch performs unpaid preflight only. (2) The job timeout rises from 20 to 60 minutes, with THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000 below the timeout and the one-hour Bedrock credential duration (role-duration-seconds 3600). Cost is bounded by BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS (default 500) and output tokens (16384). The larger budget raises potential spend on fork PRs only if BEDROCK_SCAN_ALLOW_FORKS=true, which is an explicit maintainer opt-in. The default-branch scanner checkout, persist-credentials false, pinned action SHAs, and the pull_request_target design where PR patches are treated as data are all unchanged. The merge-policy gate steps and the clearance gate are unchanged; the failure summary now says human review is required.

Remaining uncertainty: the scanner scripts (.github/scripts/threat-model-review.py, the budget and gate logic, and BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY=workload handling) were not supplied, so the claims about bounded workload calls, the deadline and human handoff are unverified. The next pass should confirm that the 500-call ceiling and the deadline are enforced in code, and that incomplete reviews cannot grant clearance.
